title: Structure for Reading, Prose for Writing: Asymmetric Structural Conditioning in Multi-Agent Document Authoring
abstract: arXiv:2608.20786v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent pipelines that author formal documents must both read a requester's forms and write against them. We report a deployed tender-response system, running an open-weights model under sovereignty constraints, and evaluate it against human-written bids the same organisation actually submitted. On a blind comparison where the system had no worked example available, an LLM judge rated its answers at least as good as the human-submitted answer on $40$ of $55$ ground-truth sections, better on $4$, missing on none, and flagged one unsupported claim in total. Classifying every gap the judge identified shows that $68\%$ were content absent from the system's own sources -- knowledge the human author held and the pipeline was never given -- so only $6$ of the $15$ adverse verdicts involve a deficiency the system could have avoided. translated_title: 阅读的结构，写作的散文：多智能体文档创作中的不对称结构条件化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.20786v1 公告类型：新 摘要：多智能体流水线在创作正式文档时，必须既要阅读请求者的表格，又要根据这些表格进行写作。我们报告了一个已部署的投标响应系统，该系统在主权约束下运行开放权重模型，并将其与同一组织实际提交的人工撰写的标书进行了评估。在系统没有可用工作示例的盲比中，一个LLM评审员在55个真实标准章节中，对40个章节的评分至少与人工提交的答案相当，在4个章节上更好，没有遗漏任何章节，并总共标记了一个无支撑的主张。对评审员识别的每个差距进行分类显示，68%的差距是系统自身来源中缺失的内容——即人类作者掌握而流水线从未获得的知识——因此15个不利裁决中只有6个涉及系统本可避免的缺陷。与真实标准的偏差更多是信息可用性问题而非写作质量问题，这是一个...
tldr: 本文提出并评估了一个多智能体投标响应系统，发现其与人工标书的差距主要源于信息缺失而非写作质量，强调了结构化阅读与写作的不对称条件化设计。
en_tdlr: This paper presents and evaluates a multi-agent tender-response system, finding that gaps versus human bids stem mainly from missing information rather than writing quality, highlighting asymmetric structural conditioning in reading and writing.
